question: Do frozen SigLIP patch embeddings plus fixed 2x2 K64 pooling preserve enough visual evidence to identify each swapped cup pair?

design.visual_frontend: Frozen SigLIP patch embedding followed by fixed 2x2 pooling from 16x16 to K=64 per frame
design.segment_encoder: One shared width-256 depth-2 factorized temporal/spatial Transformer
design.readout: One shared attention readout and three-way classifier

counterfactual_validation.condition: Roll the three swap clips by one sample within each validation batch while preserving the original labels

conclusion: The frozen patch embedding and K64 pooling preserve the swap identity perfectly. The previous recurrent failure is therefore not caused by spatial compression deleting the motion evidence. The successful probe explicitly performs temporal attention within each spatial location and spatial attention within each frame before readout; the failed M128 updater instead flattens raw segment tokens and lets memory cross-attend them without a segment-internal motion encoder. The next controlled test should initialize or prepend the proven shared swap-segment encoder before the recurrent memory update, then repeat the oracle-initial-state tracking experiment.
